correctness.rationale: When \(E\geq AD\), logistic comparison gives \(0<x\le B\). The compensator \(h(x)=2\int_0^x g_+(u)/q(u)\,du\) is finite and continuous, including at \(E=AD\). Above the threshold \(y\geq2R(B^p+C)/M\), the exact inequalities \(\dot x\le -q(x)y/2\) and \(d(\log y+h(x))/dt\le0\) give a uniform excursion bound for \(y\). For \(E<AD\), \(g(x)\geq\delta=D-E/A>0\) forces finite-time blow-up and \(1/y(t)=\int_t^Tg(x(s))\,ds\) yields \(y\geq1/[D(T-t)]\). Hence \(x=O((T-t)^\kappa)\) for some \(\kappa>0\), then \(1/y=\delta(T-t)+O((T-t)^{1+\kappa})\) and \(\dot x/x=-\nu/(T-t)+O(1+(T-t)^{\kappa-1})\). Integrability of the error establishes a strictly positive finite prey amplitude and the exact derivative exponent. All signs and boundary cases are handled analytically; exact arithmetic and finite numerical checks are diagnostic only.

value.rationale:
Finite-time explosion versus global boundedness is a central unresolved classification issue for this same group-defence model: the sharp \(E=AD\) boundary determines the behavior of every positive start. On the explosion side, the exact exponent \(
u=M/[C(D-E/A)]\) distinguishes divergent, finite nonzero, and zero prey derivative limits by the natural thresholds \(
u<1\), \(
u=1\), and \(
u>1\), while predators always blow up. This is a substantive all-data feedback estimate with direct implications for interpreting reported quenching examples, not merely a local linear or numerical observation.
